   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, December 3, 2019

   CALL TO ORDER
   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Pu
   ROLL CALL: Mayor Pu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Costanzo,
  Harrington, Liao

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. 2019 EMPLOYEE SERVICE AND RECOGNITION AWARDS
  B. INTRODUCTION OF PUBLIC WORKS INSPECTOR RAMON GUTIERREZ

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council
  on items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes.
  You will receive a 30-second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to the clerk before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please
  state your NAME for the record.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 3, 2019  2
   1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of November 19, 2019.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of November 19, 2019.
  3. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of November 21, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEE COMPLIANCE REPORT REQUIRED
  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §66006 FOR FY 2018-19

  Pursuant to Government Code §66006, a local agency which levies a fee
  subject to Government Code §66001 shall make available to the public a
  report providing the information set forth in Government Code §66006(b)(1)
  and shall review that information at the next public meeting not less than 15
  days after the information has been made available to the public. The report
  was prepared in compliance with the applicable Government Code sections
  and is hereby transmitted for City Council approval. The report was publicly
  available on the City’s website beginning November 18, 2019.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the attached Annual
  Development Impact Fee Compliance Report for FY 2018-19 in accordance
  with Government Code §66006.

  D. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-58 TO APPROVE FINANCE
  DEPARTMENT REORGANIZATION AND RELATED ACTIONS

  With recent changes within the Finance Department, the opportunity to
  reassess operations and staffing levels has presented itself. The
  recommendation provided herein reclasses one Financial Services Manager
  to Assistant Finance Director, restructures one vacant Financial Services
  Manager position to a Management Analyst, eliminates one vacant Finance
  Clerk I/II position, retitles the remaining Finance Clerk I/II position to an
  Accounting Technician I/II, and restructures the part-time Information
  Technology Specialist position to full-time. The reorganization will maintain

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 3, 2019  3
   the department’s current authorized staffing level at eight (8) full-time
  positions but provide increased operational effectiveness and approximately
  $51,600 in General Fund salary savings.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the Resolution No. 19-58,
  approving the Finance Department reorganization, the position classification
  specification and salary schedule for the Assistant Finance Director position,
  the retitling of the Finance Clerk I/II position to Accounting Technician I/II, the
  position classification specification for the Project Manager position, and the
  amended salary schedule.

  E. INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING OF AN ORDINANCE AMENDING
  TITLE III, SECTION 34 OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE – FINANCE
  AND REVENUE

  Chapter 34 – Finance and Revenue – was last amended by Ordinance No. 657
  which updated the Code regarding claims and demands, purchasing
  procedures, and informal bidding procedures. The only references to budget
  administration in the current Code are found in §31.03 – Powers and Duties
  of the City Manager – which requires the City Manager to prepare and submit
  the annual budget and capital improvement program to the City Council, and
  §32.21 Powers and Duties (Finance Department) which states that the Finance
  Department will assist with the preparation of the annual budget and
  administration thereof. The proposed Ordinance No. 660 will amend Title III,
  Section 34 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code by providing additional
  definitions, budget administration procedures, and annual audit
  requirements.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive full reading, read by title only, and introduce for first reading
  Ordinance No. 660 amending Title III, Section 34 of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code, pertaining to Budget Administration and Annual Audit;
  and
  2. Direct the City Clerk to schedule the second reading and adoption of
  Ordinance No. 660 for the next regular City Council Meeting.

  F. CERTIFIED LOCAL GOVERNMENT (CLG) PROGRAM APPLICATION

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 3, 2019  4
   The National Historic Preservation Act of 1966, as amended, provides for the
  establishment of a Certified Local Government (CLG) program to encourage
  the direct participation of local governments in the identification, evaluation,
  registration, and preservation of historic properties within their jurisdictions
  and promote the integration of local preservation interests and concerns into
  local planning and decision-making. The CLG program is a partnership among
  local governments, the State of California Office of Historic Preservation
  (OHP), and the National Park service (NPS), which responsible for
  administering the National Historic Preservation Program. Participation in the
  CLG program would support historic preservation initiatives as a means of
  increasing the economic and cultural redevelopment in the city.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-60 of the
  City Council of the City of San Gabriel, County of Los Angeles, State of
  California, authorizing the application and certification for the certified local
  government historic preservation program.

  G. INSTALLATION OF CROSSWALK MARKINGS AND SIGNAGE ON
  BROADWAY FOR SMITH PARK

  In April 2019, Public Works received a request from a resident north of Smith
  Park, requesting the installation of a mid-block pedestrian crosswalk on
  Broadway adjacent to the Smith Park swimming pool. West Broadway carries
  a moderate-to-high volume of vehicular traffic per day. Currently, there is no
  designated mid-block crossing at Smith Park on Broadway, which is an
  unusually long block. It was determined that the requested crosswalk would
  be beneficial to channelize the pedestrian crossing activity at the subject
  location were pedestrians can be seen and expected by motorists.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council accept and approve the attached mid-
  block crosswalk design sketch for construction on Broadway adjacent to
  Smith Park.

  H. PURCHASE OF TWO T3 MOTION PATROLLER ELECTRIC STANDUP
  VEHICLES AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-59 AMENDING THE
  2019-20 OPERATING BUDGET

  The current trend of police agencies is to reduce operational costs through
  fuel savings by implementing “alternative patrol vehicles.” These includes

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 3, 2019  5
   motorcycles, bicycles, Segways and T3 Motion, which are all well known for
  delivering maneuverability and cost savings in relatively small packages. The
  T3 Motion Patroller is especially gaining popularity as an alternative police
  vehicle since it specializes in the public safety sector. The purchase of two T3
  Motion Patrollers at a total cost of $28,459.05 will augment the current patrol
  fleet to achieve more effective and efficient policing in the San Gabriel
  community.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the San Gabriel Police Department implement a new
  alternative program with the purchase of two T3 Motion Patrollers for a total
  cost of $28,459.05, authorize the use of Finance Department budget savings
  to fund the equipment, and adopt Resolution No. 19-59 amending the 2019-
  20 Operating Budget by increasing the revenue estimate (transfer-in) and
  appropriations in the Capital/Special Projects Fund by $28,460.

  I. 2020 LUNAR NEW YEAR FESTIVAL

  As part of the FY 19-20 budget, the City Council allocated funding for
  community engagement events and programs. A portion of that funding is
  designated for the 6th Annual Lunar New Year Festival to be hosted by the
  City of San Gabriel on Saturday, February 8, 2020 from 11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
  in the historic Mission District. The City plans to work once again with KCM
  Agency to produce a unique event for our community, with a modern
  approach to the Lunar New Year tradition. The Professional Services
  Agreement with KCM Agency is for $30,000 base fee plus expense
  reimbursement up to an additional $52,000.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive the formal bid purchasing procedure requirement by separate
  motion; and
  2. Approve the Professional Services Agreement with KCM Agency for
  $30,000 base fee plus expense reimbursement up to an additional
  $52,000; and
  3. Authorize the transfer of $52,000 from the Non-Departmental – Citywide
  Services Contingency line-item to the Non-Departmental – Community
  Engagement Special Events line-item.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 3, 2019  6

 9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of

 10. CLOSED SESSION

 11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next Regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, January 7, 2020

  Gabriel, California. Information regarding matters to be considered at each
  meeting will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the
  City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.
